equity_bridge.item: Less H1-2026 unlevered owner FCF already reflected in the 30-Jun-2026 net debt
equity_bridge.note: Year 1 of the model is full FY2026 but net debt is 30-Jun-2026, so H1-2026 cash generation would otherwise be counted twice (once in the FY2026 flow, once as lower net debt). H1-2026 actuals (Q2-2026 interim statements): OCF C$7,817m less capital investment C$2,370m = reported FCF C$5,447m; less SBC expense C$310m; less interest income C$47m; less lease principal C$178m (treatment B charges it in the flows); plus interest expense on debt C$241m (the flows are unlevered) = ~C$5,150m. Cross-check: Dec-2025 net debt C$8,292m - C$5,150m + H1 buybacks C$1,375m + common dividends C$788m + preferred redemption C$300m = C$5,605m vs actual C$5,388m (difference is FX on USD debt, WC and other).

historical_growth.owner_fcf_basis: reported FCF (OCF - capital investment) less SBC expense less interest income, each year
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward mid-cycle: ~0.5-1% volume growth after the 2026-28 project ramp plus ~2% nominal price escalation; the historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR +4.7% diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (-9.4%) and EPS (-12.4%): the 3-yr window runs from the FY2022 oil-price peak (WTI ~US$94) to FY2025 (WTI ~US$65), so every series is a cycle artefact, not a trend. The 5-yr CAGRs (revenue +30%, equity +13.6%) start in FY2020 (COVID trough, pre-Husky) and are distorted by the Jan-2021 Husky merger. EPS 5-yr and FCF 5-yr are undefined because FY2020 EPS (-1.94) and owner FCF (-644) were negative.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF fell faster than reported FCF over FY2022-25 (SBC 373 -> 191 helps, but interest income rose 81 -> 141 as cash balances grew); the gap is small (<5% of FCF) because Cenovus's SBC is ~0.4% of revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: Mean reversion to mid-cycle. FY2026 banks the spike (H1-2026 EBITDA ~C$10bn already realized; H2 at WTI ~US$85-90), FY2027 settles at WTI US$70, and from FY2028 the model runs on WTI US$65 / WTI-WCS US$13 / C$0.72 (WCS ~C$72/bbl, about FY2025 realized pricing) escalating 2%/yr. The portfolio is the post-WRB, post-MEG entity: ~990 MBOE/d in 2027 rising to ~1,050 by 2029 as Narrows Lake, West White Rose, Sunrise and the Foster Creek optimization deliver, then ~0.5-1%/yr; mid-cycle EBITDA C$12.5-13.5bn (26-26.5% margin, structurally above the 17-21% of FY2021-25 because refining revenue left and bitumen arrived); growth capital tapers after 2028 to total capex ~C$4.7bn. Unlevered owner FCF ~C$6bn/yr mid-cycle (~12% of revenue, ~C$3.2/share) against a 12x terminal cap (~5.5x EV/EBITDA). The axes that move this case are the mid-cycle oil deck, the WTI-WCS differential (egress: TMX utilization, heavy supply from OPEC+ and Venezuela), U.S. crack spreads at Lima/Toledo/Superior, and execution on the growth projects.
scenario_narratives.bull: Elevated-for-longer. Hormuz and Middle East restart constraints hold WTI near US$90 through 2026 and US$80 in 2027, with a US$72 plateau from 2028; cracks stay wide on tight global product supply; the Canada-Alberta-industry MOU (July 2026) and the Pathways framework de-risk oil sands growth and the growth plan lands on time (~1,100 MBOE/d by 2028); synergies from MEG exceed C$400m. Margin 28-28.5% mid-cycle, 3% nominal growth. Terminal still capped at 12x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fast unwind to the bottom of the range. WTI US$55 from 2027 (OPEC+ unwind, UAE leaves OPEC, tariff slowdown), WTI-WCS US$16, cracks normalize to US$15-18. Revenue ~C$41bn, margin 21%, FCF ~C$3bn/yr (~C$1.6/share). Growth projects slip, sustaining capital is a bigger share of revenue. No solvency risk: net debt is already below the long-term target range at US$45 WTI and the preferred shares were redeemed in Q1-2026.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value an integrated oil producer on normalized, mid-cycle unlevered owner FCF, not on the cash flow a geopolitical price spike is producing today. FY2026's windfall is counted once (H1 already in June net debt, H2 in the year-1 flow), then revenue and margin are rebuilt from a WTI US$65 deck on the post-WRB, post-MEG portfolio. SBC is expensed and the share count held flat; leases are an operating cost and excluded from net debt; interest income is stripped; the terminal is capped at 12x FCF (~5.5x EV/EBITDA) because no buyer of a long-life but finite oil sands resource pays a Gordon multiple. Cyclicality is priced in the three scenario paths and their 25/50/25 weights, once, not again in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle oil deck: every US$5/bbl on WTI held in perpetuity moves mid-cycle EBITDA by roughly C$1.5bn after royalties and the value by several dollars per share -- the base US$65 is the single assumption that matters most.

WTI-WCS differential and egress: Trans Mountain utilization, heavy-crude supply (OPEC+, Venezuela policy) and U.S. heavy refining capacity; a US$3 wider differential costs ~C$1bn/yr of upstream margin, only partly recaptured by the Lloydminster Upgrader and U.S. refineries.

Growth-project execution: West White Rose ramp, Narrows Lake / Christina Lake North, Sunrise and Foster Creek optimization carry the 2027-29 volume growth and ~C$1.3bn/yr of growth capital; slippage or cost overruns push FCF out.

Downstream reliability: U.S. refining was loss-making in FY2024-25 before the WRB sale; the base case assumes Lima/Toledo/Superior and the Upgrader earn ~C$1-1.4bn/yr of operating margin at normal cracks.
Policy and carbon: the July-2026 MOU and Pathways CCS framework are not yet definitive; federal emissions cap, carbon pricing and tariff policy could raise sustaining costs.
Timing bias: discounting from a 31-Dec-2025 origin with an Oct-2026 price understates value by ~7% (~C$3/share); the Q4-2026 refresh should roll FY0 to FY2026 and remove the H1-2026 bridge item.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (CVE.TO) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 21.62-47.45. Parity: NYSE CVE (USD) x Yahoo USDCAD ties within 0.1%. WTI front-month (CL=F) and USDCAD (CAD=X) from the same API on 2026-10-09 for the H2-2026 price estimate.
data_sources.financials: CVE.TO_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2015-FY2025 annual, quarterlies to Q2-2026) via make dcf-context; Q2-2026 interim MD&A and financial statements (net debt table, lease liabilities, diluted share note, benchmark price table, 28-Jul-2026 guidance update, cash flow statement); FY2025 annual report and MD&A (WRB divestiture, MEG acquisition, 10-Dec-2025 guidance deck, lease maturity table, SBC expense, interest income, cash taxes paid).
data_sources.qualitative: No CVE.TO_Analysis.json existed at build time; scenario axes come from the Q2-2026 MD&A commodity outlook and policy sections and the FY2025 MD&A strategy section.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, Stock-Based Compensation Expense (Recovery) C$191m (consolidated statement of earnings / Note). Awards are mostly cash-settled and revalued each period, so the expense swings with the share price (FY2017 -6, FY2022 373, H1-2026 310). The cash-flow add-back 'Stock-Based Compensation, Net of Payments' was only C$163m in FY2025 because C$28m was cash-settled inside OCF; the full expense is deducted here (C$28m more conservative). No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis).
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,849.5m common shares outstanding at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2-2026 MD&A, includes 4.8m held by the employee benefit Trust) plus 11.1m dilutive effect of stock-based compensation from the Q2-2026 diluted EPS note (1,871.2m diluted weighted average vs 1,860.1m basic). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Buybacks are funded (C$1,995m FY2025; C$1,375m H1-2026 for 37.7m shares; a further 5.6m shares to 24-Jul-2026), so the flat count is paid for, not a convention. The count is 1,844.2m at 24-Jul-2026 and falling; using the 30-Jun figure is consistent with the 30-Jun net debt.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and quote are both CAD; no conversion. Parity check: NYSE CVE in USD x Yahoo USDCAD (1.4254, 2026-10-09) ties to the TSX quote within 0.1%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the currency of the flows. Government of Canada 10-year ~3.4% (Oct-2026), equity risk premium 5.0%, levered beta ~1.3 for an integrated oil & gas producer -> cost of equity ~9.9%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (BBB+/A- senior notes), ~3.7% after tax at 24%. Market-value weights ~90% equity / ~10% debt (C$83bn market cap vs C$5.4bn net debt + C$3.1bn leases) -> WACC 9.3%. Used in ALL THREE scenarios: oil-price cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows (bear WTI US$55 / bull US$72-80) and in the 12x terminal cap, not in the discount rate, so no premium is stacked on top (adaptations rule f, charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Lease liabilities of C$3,073m at 30-Jun-2026 (C$383m current + C$2,690m non-current, Q2-2026 balance sheet) are EXCLUDED from net debt. The full lease cash cost -- principal (C$178m H1-2026, ~C$355m/yr) plus interest on lease liabilities (C$90m H1-2026, ~C$180m/yr), ~C$535m/yr in total, matching the C$519m 2026 contractual figure in the FY2025 maturity table -- is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (flat in dollars, so the percentage rises as revenue normalizes). The da_pct_path is ex right-of-use depreciation (~C$350m/yr) so the lease is not charged twice; cash tax is never credited on a loss.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is C$16m at 30-Jun-2026 (0.05% of equity) -- immaterial. Deducted once in the equity bridge for completeness; the flows are not adjusted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row: operating company, non-US and cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Cenovus is an integrated oil & gas producer (oil sands SAGD, conventional, Atlantic/Asia-Pacific offshore, Canadian upgrading and U.S. refining) whose value is a stream of free cash flow; none of the non-FCF routes apply. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no Analysis JSON yet -- scenario axes are drawn from the Q2-2026 and FY2025 MD&A). CYCLICAL NORMALIZATION: H1-2026 and spot prices are a geopolitical spike (U.S.-Iran conflict / Strait of Hormuz: Q2-2026 WTI US$92.79, Q1-2026 US$71.93, Q2-2025 US$63.74; WTI front-month ~US$92 on 2026-10-09). Management's own 10-Dec-2025 planning deck was WTI US$60 / WCS US$47.50 / C$0.72, and its balance-sheet framework targets net debt <= C$4bn at WTI US$45. The base case therefore carries FY2026 near the spike (H1 actual + H2 at ~US$85-90), reverts to WTI US$70 in FY2027 and a mid-cycle WTI US$65 / WTI-WCS US$13 / USDCAD 0.72 (WCS ~C$72/bbl, roughly FY2025 realized pricing) from FY2028, then escalates ~2%/yr. PORTFOLIO PRO-FORMA: FY2025 revenue (C$49,696m) includes nine months of the WRB refineries (238.7 Mbbl/d, divested 30-Sep-2025 for C$1.9bn) and only 1.5 months of MEG Energy (~105 kbbl/d bitumen, acquired 13-Nov-2025 for cash + 143.9m shares). Mid-cycle revenue of the current portfolio is ~C$47-48bn at ~990 MBOE/d (H1-2026 revenue re-priced to the mid-cycle deck), and the EBITDA margin is structurally higher (~26%) than the 17-21% of FY2021-25 because low-margin refining revenue left and high-margin bitumen arrived; cross-checked two ways (FY2025 EBITDA C$10.2bn + MEG full-year ~C$1.5bn incl. C$400m synergies + growth barrels + normalized downstream ~C$1bn; and H1-2026 EBITDA ~C$10.0bn re-priced to WCS C$72 net of royalty relief) both land at C$12.5-13.5bn mid-cycle. TIMING / DOUBLE-COUNT GUARD: the balance sheet and share count are 30-Jun-2026 (latest filing) while year 1 is full-year FY2026; the H1-2026 cash flow that already reduced June net debt from C$8,292m to C$5,388m is therefore removed in the equity_bridge (see that note) so it is not counted in both the flows and the bridge. Discounting is end-of-year from a 31-Dec-2025 origin although the price is Oct-2026, a ~7% (~C$3/share) conservative bias shared by every December-year-end ticker valued late in its year on this engine. Reported FCF is OCF less capital investment and is AFTER interest paid (~C$381m FY2025) because Cenovus classifies interest in operating activities; the forward build is unlevered, so last_fcf is a levered anchor and understates the year-1 base slightly. Working capital capture is 0: commodity receivables/inventory swing with price and net out over the cycle (the C$546m H1-2026 build sits in the June balance sheet and will release as prices fall). Growth outlook per 2026 guidance updated 28-Jul-2026: production 970-1,010 MBOE/d, capital C$5.0-5.3bn (sustaining C$3.5-3.6bn, growth C$1.2-1.4bn on Christina Lake North/Narrows Lake, West White Rose, Sunrise, Lloydminster), heading toward ~1,050-1,100 MBOE/d by 2028, after which growth capital tapers. Terminal value: 12x cap binds in every scenario (Gordon at 9.3%/2.0% is 14.0x); 12x FCF equals ~5.5x terminal EV/EBITDA, in line with where Canadian oil sands producers have traded.

bear.narrative: The spike unwinds fast: WTI ~US$75 in H2-2026 (FY2026 ~C$57.6bn), then US$55 from FY2027 as OPEC+ fully unwinds cuts, the UAE's exit from OPEC adds supply and a tariff-driven slowdown dents demand; the WTI-WCS differential widens to US$16 as TMX fills. Revenue ~C$41bn, margin 21-22% (royalty relief offsets only part of the netback loss, cost inflation sticks). West White Rose and Sunrise ramp late; sustaining capital of C$3.6bn plus committed growth spend is a larger share of a smaller revenue base (10.5-11.5%). Cash flow still covers the dividend; the balance-sheet framework (net debt <= C$4bn at US$45 WTI) means no solvency question, so the bear is a value case, not a survival case.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 ~C$61.6bn = H1 actual C$29.8bn + H2 ~C$31.8bn at WTI ~US$85-90 fading. FY2027 WTI US$70 (partial reversion; OPEC+ unwind, Middle East restarts): mid-cycle revenue ~C$47.7bn x (70/65)^0.9 = ~C$51bn. FY2028 WTI US$65 with +4% production (West White Rose, Narrows Lake, Sunrise) ~C$49.6bn. FY2029-30 +2.5%/+1.5% volume plus 2% price escalation; FY2031-35 2.5% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 30%: H1-2026 EBITDA ~C$10.0bn (34%) + H2 ~C$8.5-9bn at lower cracks. FY2027 27.5% at WTI 70. From FY2028 26%, rising to 26.5% as high-margin SAGD barrels and the remaining MEG synergies (C$400m/yr by 2028) land: C$12.9bn EBITDA on C$49.6bn. Historical 17-21% (FY2021-25) was diluted by WRB refining revenue.
base.capex_rationale: 2026 guidance C$5.0-5.3bn (8.4%); 2027 ~C$5.1bn with growth projects still in flight (10%); 2028+ growth capital tapers to ~C$0.7bn, sustaining rises with production to ~C$3.9bn, total ~C$4.7bn escalating with revenue (9.5%). Long-run capex (9.5%) below D&A (12%) because D&A carries acquisition step-ups from Husky and MEG.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 24%: Canadian statutory 23% (15% federal + 8% Alberta), U.S. refining 21% + state, Asia-Pacific higher. FY2025 cash taxes paid C$1,225m on pre-tax C$4,477m = 27%; FY2024 21%; FY2023 51% (catch-up instalments on FY2022). The FY2025 12.2% effective rate is a non-taxable WRB CTA reclassification, not a repeatable rate.

bull.narrative: Hormuz constraints and slow Middle East restarts keep WTI ~US$90 through H2-2026 (FY2026 ~C$63.6bn), US$80 in FY2027, and a US$72 plateau from FY2028 escalating 2%/yr; the July-2026 Canada-Alberta-industry MOU and Pathways CCS framework unlock the growth plan on schedule (production +5%/yr to ~1,100 MBOE/d by 2028). Margin 28-28.5% mid-cycle. Capex held at 9% as growth capital is spent but on a larger revenue base.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house default 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: oil is at a geopolitical high (front-month ~US$92 vs a US$60 planning deck ten months ago) and the single largest driver of value is a commodity price whose historical norm is mean reversion; the stock sits within 6% of its 52-week high after a ~100% run from the low, so the downside path is live. Bull down to 25%: it requires the geopolitical premium to persist for two to three years AND on-schedule execution of four growth projects AND regulatory reform to land -- several independent things going right. No going-concern or covenant element argues for a higher bear weight: net debt/AFF was 0.4x at June 2026.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
